description: We're a team of students from GFS!
summary:
Together, we built a web app that can be used to investigate surface change anywhere on Earth using real data from NISAR, the NASA-ISRO radar satellite. The interface is simple, interactive, and engaging: a user picks a location on a map, and the app finds the NISAR observations covering it. It then displays the respective "before" and "after" satellite maps alongside comparative exportable statistics, charts, and smart explanations that illustrate the surface change in a palatable format. 
GFS_NISAR translates incredibly valuable NISAR data that can be used to track changes such as deforestation, flooding, and land movement. But that value only reaches people if the data is approachable. By lowering the barrier, the tool lets researchers, conservation groups, journalists, and curious students explore environmental change themselves. Its transparent treatment of uncertainty also models good scientific practice rather than overclaiming.
details:
GFS_NISAR is a website that lets any user select a specific location and see how the surface has changed over time using NISAR data. Users pick a location on a map model, and the site finds every NISAR observation in that area. It then groups the observations based on the satellite’s viewpoint - so that only images from the same angles are compared - and finds suitable before-and-after observations to compare. We analysed the differences between the before-and-after observations, focusing on the polarization values (HV and HH) to conclude the changes in the surface.

Impact: With easy-to-understand explanations and interactive formats, our tool is accessible to everyone, no matter their expertise level. We hope that our tool helps students, researchers, journalists, communities, and the general public explore real satellite data and see for themselves how our planet is changing, making it a tool that helps us achieve satellite monitoring as an everyday resource rather than something only experts can use, so that changes to the Earth’s surface are noticed sooner and acted on faster.

Benefits: NISAR files are technical and hard to understand without expertise. Our tool handles the searching, processing, and comparison automatically, then presents the results as plain-language explanations that anyone can understand. Users can see more than just a change. They see where, when, and by how much.

Tools Used:

Languages: TypeScript / JavaScript, Python 3.14, HTML5, CSS3, YAML/JSON

Python / scientific libraries: NumPy, Pandas, Rasterio (GDAL), harmony-py, requests, asf_search, earthaccess, h5py, pyproj, Pillow, pytest

Services/Data/APIs: NASA NISAR L2 GCOV, NASA CMR, ASF (Alaska Satellite Facility), NASA Harmony, NASA Earthdata, Google Gemini API, OpenStreetMap

Software & tools: Git, GitHub, Node.js 24, npm, vsc, Python venv, free-tier Gemini AI, Chrome DevTools (headless CDP), Render hosting

How it's creative: The AI explanations connect the radar measurements to real-world meaning, so users don’t just see a map of change but understand why it matters and what to do next. It works for any location NISAR covers, not just one fixed example. It also measures all surface changes.

Factors Considered: Accessibility - Legends and explanations so non-experts can understand the data. Fair comparisons - Only comparing images taken from the same viewpoint, so differences are more accurate and a real change is measured.

(Project takes around 30 seconds to load)
